clue.text: Unhappy place in Northern Ireland

definitions.meaning: unhappy means low in spirits, miserable or dejected
a county on the east coast, one of the six counties of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone feels miserable about a particular spot in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland, on its east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: low in spirits, and the name of a Northern Irish county.

clue.text: Expresses disapproval, things being what they are

definitions.meaning: a person who protests or complains is raising a protest
items or articles are physical bodies, things that simply are what they are

explanation.surface: Someone protests about the way of the world, resigned to circumstances as they stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Things being what they are' sounds like a resigned idiom, but 'things' is the second definition and 'being what they are' just reinforces it.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means protests; as a plural noun it means physical items or articles.

clue.text: A god reluctant, surprisingly, to be praised

indicators.note: surprisingly hints the letters of these three words turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A deity who is unwilling, against expectation, to receive acclaim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges the thirteen letters of A GOD RELUCTANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To congratulate someone is to commend or praise them for an achievement.

clue.text: Greek character tense for the most part

indicators.note: for the most part asks for most of the word, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: tense, as of a rope pulled tight, means taut

explanation.surface: A letter of the Greek alphabet is mostly nervy, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' cuts the last T from TAUT.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the nineteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, equivalent to our T.

clue.text: Teacher sitting in drab bistro

indicators.note: sitting in says the letters are seated inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A teacher is seated in a dull little cafe.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish religious leader is literally a teacher of the law; the title means master.

clue.text: Cheers smart session of the wine club?

parts.note: ta is an informal British thank-you, as is cheers
to smart is to sting, as a cut or a slap does

explanation.surface: A toast is raised at a fashionable gathering of wine lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' looks like a toast but means thanks, giving TA; 'smart' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to sting.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine club meets to sample wines; the question mark flags this definition by example.

clue.text: Design of unusual tunic, old, with edge worn away

indicators.note: unusual says the following letters are set in an out-of-the-ordinary order
with edge worn away loses the final letter of the word old

explanation.surface: A pattern on a strange old tunic whose hem has frayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with edge worn away' trims OLD to OL; 'unusual' then rearranges TUNIC with OL.
explanation.definitionFit: A print made from a carved block of linoleum is a design or artwork.

clue.text: Fury of fisherman when lake has been blocked off

indicators.note: blocked off means shut out, so the lake's letter is removed from the fisherman

parts.note: an angler is someone who fishes with rod and line
L is the standard map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: An angler is furious because the lake he fishes has been closed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has been blocked off' removes L (lake) from ANGLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Fury and rage are synonyms for intense displeasure.

clue.text: Pub drink of light hue, lacking a head

indicators.note: lacking a head means the first letter is taken away

parts.note: a light shade is a pale one; the letters running backwards across 'hue lacking' are a coincidence, not the setter's device

explanation.surface: A pale beer poured flat, with no froth on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking a head' drops the P from PALE; the head of a beer is its froth, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer of this kind is the classic drink served in a British pub.

clue.text: Where you could find cops in a toilet possibly?

definitions.text: Where you could find cops in a toilet possibly?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the phrase could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Police officers lurking in a public lavatory — where else might one find them?
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges COPS IN A TOILET; the whole clue doubles as the definition of where officers are based.
explanation.definitionFit: Officers work from this building, so it is where you would expect to find them.

clue.text: Unfair treatment, providing unseasoned wood

parts.note: unseasoned timber is raw, not yet dried out
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: A buyer is cheated by being supplied with green, undried timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unseasoned' suggests cooking but here describes timber not yet dried, and deal is softwood planking.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a harsh or unjust arrangement someone has to put up with.

clue.text: Greek character needs help, first to last

indicators.note: first to last says the opening letter is shifted to the end

parts.note: to abet is to help, usually in wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A Greek person needs assistance, going from first in line to last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' moves the A of ABET to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the second letter of the Greek alphabet, matching our B.

clue.text: Old actor excited — honorary degree being this?

indicators.note: excited suggests the letters are stirred up into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A veteran thespian is thrilled at being given an honorary degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges OLD ACTOR. An honorary doctorate is the degree an old actor might receive.
explanation.definitionFit: An honorary doctorate is a degree of the highest, PhD level, hence describable by this adjective.

clue.text: Snake is something you can't see

definitions.meaning: to snake is to twist and turn, as a road does
moving air, a breeze, is invisible

explanation.surface: An invisible serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means meander like a snake; as a noun it is moving air, felt but never seen.

clue.text: Choose not to participate in work with illegal salesman?

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
a ticket tout sells tickets unofficially at inflated prices

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to take part in a job with a dodgy trader.
explanation.walkthrough: A tout resells tickets, often illegally; the question mark admits he is not always a lawbreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb for withdrawing or declining to join in.

clue.text: Old Roman juries — casual, slack

indicators.note: slack suggests loose and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman complains that juries are casual and lax.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous general and dictator of Rome, assassinated in 44 BC.

clue.text: Conservative circle has dined inside — this being provided?

indicators.note: inside puts the eating word within the circle word

parts.note: ate is what someone did who has dined

explanation.surface: A Tory club has eaten in, and wonders whether food will be supplied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' places the dining word right after the C, splitting the Conservative circle. The definition leans on the whole surface: food laid on for diners at a party function.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplying food and drink at a function is what this trade does.

clue.text: Team is one of four on the square

definitions.meaning: a group of players in a match, an eleven

definitions.text: one of four on the square

explanation.surface: A team is one of four sides contesting on the town square.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporting team, and one edge of a four-sided figure.

clue.text: Ring up where it's generally pretty cold

definitions.text: Ring up where it's generally pretty cold

parts.words: Ring up where it's generally pretty cold
parts.note: a ring is a circle, and up north in the polar region is where it is cold

explanation.surface: Phone someone in a place that is usually chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring up' looks like making a phone call, but it means a ring located far up north.
explanation.definitionFit: The line of latitude encircling the north polar region, a ring high on the globe.

clue.text: Bribe to acquire a menial dwelling

parts.note: a bung is British slang for a bribe

explanation.surface: Someone pays a bribe to get a humble little house.
explanation.walkthrough: A bung is British slang for a bribe or backhander.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-storey house is a type of dwelling.

clue.text: Growing area — one with a tree or shrub

parts.note: a garden is where plants are grown
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A plot for growing things, with a single tree or bush in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering evergreen plant of the madder family, grown as a bush or small tree.

clue.text: Hanging decoration made with fancy slates

indicators.note: fancy suggests something elaborate, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ornament fashioned from ornate roof slates.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuft of threads tied at one end, dangling as ornament.

clue.text: Pole in box

definitions.meaning: a stout pole such as a mast or boom on a ship
to box is to fight with the fists, as in practice

explanation.surface: A post inside a crate.
explanation.definitionFit: A stout pole on a ship, and to box in practice bouts.

clue.text: Pleasant French resort

definitions.meaning: the Riviera city on the Côte d'Azur

explanation.surface: An agreeable seaside town in France.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for agreeable, and the Mediterranean city in southern France.
